newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World names convertible bond arranger.
newsitem.headline: New World names convertible bond arranger.

text.p: New World Development Co Ltd said on Monday it had appointed HSBC Investment Bank Asia Ltd as global co-ordinator for a proposed issue of US$300 million guaranteed bonds convertible into shares of New World China Ltd.
New World China, a wholly owned subsidiary of New World, was formed to hold and manage certain property development and investment interests of the company and its units in China.

The bonds are automatically convertible into New World China shares on the occasion of an initial public offering (IPO) of the shares on the Hong Kong or other recognised stock exchange on or before Dec 31, 1999, it said.
The conversion price per share would be equal to the IPO price less a yet-to-be decided discount, New World said in a statement.
It was expected that in the absence of an IPO, the bonds would be redeemable at on December 31, 1999 at a premium to the principal amount.
HSBC, which is also the bookrunner and lead manager of the proposed issue, will be granted an option to require the issuer to increase the issue to cover over-allotments, it said.
The net proceeds of the issue were intended to be used to finance the group's property development and investment activities in China and for general working capital.
The terms of the issue were expected to be finalised around the end of the month.
The company said it had filed an application to list the bonds on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.
